text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The stolen body of late business magnate Vehbi Koc body was found in the cemetery it had disappeared from in October. Five people who stole the corpse to demand a ransom from Koc's family were arrested.
- Turkey will not tolerate Greeek Cypriot decision to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia. Ankara warns Greek Cypriot government that it could shoot the missile launch pads.
- The cabinet approves 30 percent pension rise for retired workers registered to the SSK (Social Security Board), one of three state pension funds.
- The government wants to sell state properties and land to foreigners. Municipalities will be given full authority to sell public real estate.
- Prosecutor prepares documents to lift the immunity of former interior minister Mehmet Agar and government MP Sedat Bucak for their involvement in a security scandal.
- Murdered leftist journalist Metin Goktepe was commemorated on the first anniversary of his death.
- Treasury undersecretary says foreign capital regards Turkey as having good investment potential.
- Government kicks off effort to industrialise eastern Turkey.
